sanskrit: śivās te santv oṣadhīr apakrītāḥ sahīyasīr vīrudho yā abhiṣṭutāḥ | apāṃ sarasvatīṃ jyeṣṭhāṃ trāyantām asmākaṃ gām aśvaṃ puruṣaṃ paśum ||
english: Benign be to you the herbs, the purchased ones, the mightier plants, the creepers that have been invoked with praise; may Sarasvatī, the eldest of the waters, protect our cattle, our horse, our man, our beast.

sanskrit: madhuman mūlaṃ madhumad agram āsāṃ madhuman madhyaṃ vīrudhāṃ babhūva | madhumat parṇaṃ madhumat puṣpam āsāṃ madhoḥ saṃbhūtā amṛtasya bhakṣo ghṛtam annaṃ duhrate gopurogavam ||
english: Honey-sweet the root, honey-sweet the tip of these plants has become; honey-sweet the middle of the creepers; honey-sweet their leaf, honey-sweet their flower — born of sweetness, they are a taste of immortality; they yield ghee and food for the herd of cattle led by the bull.

sanskrit: yāvatīḥ kīyatīś cemāḥ pṛthivyām adhy oṣadhīḥ | tā naḥ sahasraparṇyo mṛtyor muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: However many, however numerous these herbs that grow upon the earth — may they, with their thousand leaves, release us from the distress of death.

sanskrit: vaiyāghro maṇir vīrudhāṃ trāyamāṇo 'bhiśastipāḥ | amīvāḥ sarvā rakṣāṃsy apa hantv adhi dūram asmat ||
english: The tiger-amulet, the gem of plants, the guardian that wards off curses — may it drive far away from us all diseases and all demons.

sanskrit: siṃhasyeva stanathor oṣadhīnām agner iva vijanta ābhṛtābhyaḥ | gavāṃ yakṣmaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ vīrudbhir atinutto nāvyā etu srotyāḥ ||
english: As the roar of a lion, as the blazing of fire scatters what was gathered against the herbs — the wasting disease of cattle and of men, chased off by the plants, shall flow away like a navigable river into a river channel.

sanskrit: mumucānā oṣadhayo agner vaiśvānarād adhi | bhūmiṃ saṃtanvatīr ita yāsāṃ rājā vanaspatiḥ ||
english: Loosed forth from Vaiśvānara, the all-consuming fire, the herbs spread themselves over the earth from here — they whose king is the lord of the forest.

sanskrit: yāś cāhaṃ veda vīrudho yāś ca paśyāmi cakṣuṣā | ajñātā jānīmaś ca yā yāsu vidmasi saṃbhṛtam | sarvāḥ samagrā oṣadhīr bodhantu vacaso mama ||
english: The creepers that I know and those that I see with my eyes, those unknown ones that we may come to know, those in which we know healing to be gathered — may all herbs, complete and entire, heed my utterance.

sanskrit: yā rohanty āṅgirasīḥ parvateṣu sameṣu ca vīrudho viśvabheṣajīḥ | tā no mayasvatīḥ śivā oṣadhīḥ santu śaṃ hṛde ||
english: The Āṅgirasa plants, the universal-healing creepers that grow on mountains and on level grounds — may those herbs, full of delight, benign, be a blessing to our heart.

sanskrit: aśvattho darbho vīrudhāṃ somo rājāmṛtaṃ haviḥ | vrīhir yavaś ca bheṣajau divas putrāv amartyau ||
english: The aśvattha, the darbha among the creepers, King Soma the immortal oblation; rice and barley are two healers, the two immortal sons of heaven.

sanskrit: uj jīhīdhve stanayaty abhikrandanty oṣadhīḥ | yadā vaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ parjanyo retasāvati ||
english: Rise up, you herbs, as it thunders and roars — when Parjanya, rich in seed, waters you, O speckle-mothered ones.

sanskrit: tasyāmṛtasyemaṃ balaṃ puruṣaṃ pārayāmasi | atho kṛṇomi bheṣajaṃ yathāsac chatahāyanaḥ ||
english: By that immortal power we bring this man across to safety; and I make a remedy so that he may live a hundred years.

sanskrit: varāho veda vīrudhaṃ nakulo veda bheṣajīḥ | gandharvāḥ sarpā yā vidus tā ihā yantv oṣadhīḥ ||
english: The boar knows the healing plant; the mongoose knows the medicinal herbs; whatever herbs the Gandharvas and the serpents know — let those herbs come here.

sanskrit: yāḥ suparṇā āṅgirasīr divyā yā raghaṭo viduḥ | vayāṃsi haṃsā yā vidur yāś ca sarve patatriṇaḥ | mṛgā yā vidur oṣadhīs tā asmā avase huve ||
english: Those that the suparṇas know, the heavenly Āṅgirasa plants that the raghaṭa bird knows; those that the birds, the haṃsas know, and all the flying creatures; the herbs that the deer know — those I call hither to give him aid.

sanskrit: yāvatīnām oṣadhīnāṃ gāvaḥ prāśnanty aghnyā yāvatīnām ajāvayaḥ | tāvatīr viśvabheṣajīr ā bharāmi tvām abhi ||
english: As many herbs as the inviolable cows graze upon, as many as the goats and sheep graze upon — of that many kinds of universal-healing herbs I bring a full measure toward you.

sanskrit: yāvatīṣu manuṣyā bheṣajaṃ bhiṣajo viduḥ | tāvatīs tubhyam ābhṛtāḥ śarma yacchantv oṣadhīḥ ||
english: In as many herbs as human healers know a remedy — may herbs of that many kinds, brought to you, bestow shelter upon you.

sanskrit: puṣpavatīḥ prasūmatīḥ phalinīr aphalā uta | saṃmātara iva duhrām asmā ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: Those that are in flower, those that have given birth, those bearing fruit, and those without fruit — like mothers uniting together, let them give milk to him for the sake of his unharmed wholeness.

sanskrit: ut tvāhārṣaṃ pañcaśalād ut tvā daśaśalād uta | ut tvā yamasya paḍvīśād oṣadhībhir apīparam ||
english: I have raised you out of the five-fettered snare, and out of the ten-fettered snare as well; I have lifted you out of Yama's foot-fetter — with the herbs I have brought you safely across.

sanskrit: indrasya prathamo ratho devānām aparo ratho varuṇasya tṛtīya it | ahīnām apamā ratha sthāṇum ārad athā riṣat ||
english: The first chariot belongs to Indra; the next chariot belongs to the gods; Varuṇa's is truly the third. The last chariot is that of the serpents — it has come near to the post; let it then strike.

sanskrit: darbhaḥ śocis tarūṇakam aśvasya vāraḥ puruṣasya vāraḥ | rathasya bandhuram ahīnām arasaṃ viṣaṃ vār id ugram ||
english: The darbha grass is the flame, the tender shoot; it is the shield of the horse, the shield of the man; it is the cross-bar of the chariot — the venom of the serpents is made powerless; indeed it is a mighty ward.

sanskrit: ava śveta padā jahi pūrveṇa cāpareṇa ca | udaplutam iva dārv ahīnām arasaṃ viṣaṃ vār id ugram ||
english: O white one, strike down with your fore-hoof and with your hind-hoof alike; like a piece of wood that has been soaked in water, the venom of the serpents is made powerless — indeed it is a mighty ward.

sanskrit: araṃghaso nimajya- -unmajya punar abravīt | udaplutam iva dārv ahīnām arasaṃ viṣaṃ vār id ugram ||
english: Araṃghasa, having plunged and emerged again, spoke once more: like a piece of wood that has been soaked in water, the venom of the serpents is made powerless — indeed it is a mighty ward.

sanskrit: paidvo hanti kaṣarṇīlaṃ paidvaḥ śvitram utāsitam | paidvo ratharvyāḥ śiraḥ saṃ bibheda pṛdākvāḥ ||
english: Paidva slays the kaṣarṇīla serpent; Paidva slays the white one and the dark one; Paidva has shattered the head of the ratharvyā, of the spotted snake.

sanskrit: paidva prehi prathamo anu tvā vayam emasi | ahīn vy asyatāt patho yena smā vayam emasi ||
english: O Paidva, go forth first; we shall follow after you. Drive the serpents away from the path along which we shall travel.

sanskrit: idaṃ paidvo ajāyata- -idam asya parāyaṇam | imāny arvataḥ padā- -ahighnyo vājinīvataḥ ||
english: Here Paidva was born; here is his domain. These are the hoofprints of the steed, of Vājinīvat, the serpent-slayer.

sanskrit: saṃyataṃ na vi ṣparad vyāttaṃ na saṃ yamat | asmin kṣetre dvāv ahī strī ca pumāṃś ca tā ubhā arasā ||
english: What is shut let it not spring open; what is open let it not shut tight. In this field there are two serpents, a female and a male — both of them are rendered venomless.

sanskrit: arasāsa ihāhayo ye anti ye ca dūrake | ghanena hanmi vṛścikam ahiṃ daṇḍenāgatam ||
english: Venomless are the serpents here, those near and those far away. With a club I strike the scorpion; the serpent that has come I strike with the staff.

sanskrit: aghāśvasyedaṃ bheṣajam ubhayoḥ svajasya ca | indro mahyam aghāyantam ahiṃ paidvo arundhayat ||
english: This is the remedy of Aghāśva, for both kinds of serpent and for the constrictor as well; Indra and Paidva have restrained for me the serpent that seeks to do evil.
